What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0194-0051 showed the wellhead at 24.8 °C with the air at 19.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 15 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0194-028

Asset: WELL-0194 (NE-08 Well 194, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 30 Aug 2025 12:00 · Well stopped for this job: 28 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0194-0146 on 2025-08-28 Report written: 30 Aug 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0194-0146 at 09:45 on 2025-08-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 9.8% of the pad area, estimated 2.1 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.3 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 5 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 198 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 158 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

Maintenance Report — MNT-0194-031

Asset: WELL-0194 (NE-08 Well 194, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 11 Feb 2026 17:00 · Well stopped for this job: 297 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0194-0168 on 2026-01-29 Report written: 12 Feb 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0194-0168 showed the wellhead at 11.6 °C with the air at 9.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 10 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0194-031 (WS-06).
